I've opened [PR #947](https://github.com/acme/omni/pull/947). On the QA stack, a thread opened by an agent seated in a #conductor thread now nests under that #conductor thread in the rail, on desktop web, the 390px phone layout and the desktop app.

## Root cause
- **Where the parent is set:** every way a seated agent opens a thread files it under the agent's hidden seat thread. `omni new` sends `OMNI_THREAD_ID` (`crates/omni-cli/src/commands/write.rs:88`, `:98`). `delegate` and `delegate_team` send `SELF` (`apps/mcp/omni.ts:428`, `:471`). The server fills in the caller as parent (`apps/server/thread-routes-api.ts:247`).
- **Why it vanished:** the side rail, Inbox and Activity all build their tree from the channel list, and that list grouped threads by their raw parent (`apps/server/channels-api.ts:162`, `threads.conductorHandoffChildren`). So the group's parent was the hidden seat, which no list shows. The child was still treated as nested, so it appeared nowhere.
- **T-AEAF before and after:** its `parent_id` stays `c97c54e0` (the seat). Its rail group moves from `c97c54e0` to `2895609f`. This thread moves from seat `704eeec4` to `8c7b5bd9`. T-610A stays under `488bd97a`.

## What I chose and why
- I fixed it where the list is built: a child whose parent is a #conductor seat is grouped under the seat's #conductor thread. Every surface builds its tree from that list, including iOS, so no client code changed.
- I left `parent_id` on the seat. Crew reports go to a thread's parent, and that is what wakes the seated agent to relay the report (set up in #940). Moving the parent to the #conductor thread would send reports to the Conductor instead.

## Backfill
- No migration was needed and none ran, because the fix applies whenever the list is read. Rows written: 0.
- On this machine, 8 existing threads move under their #conductor thread, including T-AEAF and this one (T-889E). That happens once the live install runs a release that includes #947. I did not touch the live server on :4747.

## Tests
- New case in `apps/server/tests/channel-handoffs.test.ts`:
  - work opened from a seat lists under the visible #conductor thread, not the seat;
  - when filed in a folder, it still shows in the folder and keeps the seat as parent;
  - an archived job drops its group.

  It fails on `main` and passes here.
- `apps/server/tests/team.test.ts` now opens the seated agent's thread into a folder. It checks the nesting, then the existing check that the crew report comes back and the seated agent relays it. Both files: 13 of 13 pass.
- Full suite, with the `OMNI_*`/`APNS_*` variables unset: `npx turbo run test --concurrency=2 --continue --force` passed 8 of 8 packages (server: 4022 passed, 6 skipped).
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run unused` and `npx turbo boundaries` pass.

## Screenshots
These are in the thread's artifacts folder and in the PR:
- `desktop-before.png`, `desktop-after.png`: rail Inbox panel. Before, the job shows as Working with nothing under it; after, "Cursor harness parity…" sits under it.
- `phone-before.png`, `phone-after.png`: 390px Activity.
- `desktop-app-after.png`: desktop app QA harness. There's no before shot here; it shows the same Web UI from the same list, so it matches desktop web's before.

## Docs
ADR 0019 and `docs/user/threads.md` each gained a sentence on where this thread shows.

The merge-risk gate hadn't rated #947 when I stopped. It checks PRs on a timer and will post its rating on the PR and in this thread.
title: Fix seat thread parent_id so nested threads show under Conductor
